title: River stage at one constant rating keeps the pre-1957 runoff excess and the post-1997 south-east Australian deficit; early ratings gave less flood flow per unit stage (49 BoM gauges, 1885-2021)
abstract: Question: long Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) flow records show runoff at equal rain about 20-30% higher before 1957 than in 1957-1996 (mostly flood flows) and 12-17% lower in south-east Australia (SE-AU) since about 2010. Six earlier campaign bundles said that flow measurement (stage-discharge ratings, extrapolated at high flows) could cause these changes but could not be tested. Do the changes remain when the river-stage record is converted to discharge with one constant rating? Approach: BoM Water Data Online stores measured stage beside published discharge back to 1885-1950. For 58 long-record gauges (49 used: 31 SE-AU, 18 North; 29 with pre-1957 data) we downloaded both as-stored series. A quarterly anchor stage at a fixed mid flow removes datum and low-flow control changes; the 1957-1996 median applied rating converts every stored stage value to constant-rating (CR) discharge. Per gauge, annual runoff was regressed on rain and previous-year rain (CAMELS-AUS SILO, AGCD) over 1957-1996; departures in % of mean flow; 2x2-degree cell bootstrap. Plan written before results. Results: the pre-1957 excess was +30.4% (95% CI +19.9 to +40.8) published and +42.9% (+28.3 to +60.2) at constant rating (29 gauges; SE-AU +23.8 and +31.1). The SE-AU 2010-2021 deficit was -14.1% (-23.0 to -7.4) published and -13.2% (-21.3 to -7.7) at constant rating; rating effect -0.8 (-3.9 to +1.6). Before 1937, applied ratings gave 18-20% less discharge above the 1957-1996 Q99 at equal relative stage than modern ratings, and not more in any era or flow band; after 1997 ratings agree within a few percent. Decisions held for anchors at 10/25/50% exceedance, reference ratings 1975-1996 and 1997-2021, AGCD rain, square-root and flood-part models; extrapolated volume was 0% at the median gauge. Conclusion: rating changes do not explain the pre-1957 excess or the post-1997 deficit; both are in the stage record. Limitations: archived ratings may be re-computed; a rating difference can be an error or a correct rating for channel change (then CR overstates the early excess); 29 early gauges in 14 cells; annual linear models.

citations.reason: We use its 58 long-record gauges and test whether its pre-1957 excess and post-1997 deficit are rating artefacts; both remain at constant rating.
We use its gauge list; it named extrapolated early ratings as the remaining untested cause of the pre-1957 excess, which we test and exclude.
It found that the 1937-1960 high era was a flood-flow excess and listed ratings as untested; the flood excess remains at constant rating.
Its open question was catchment change or rating drift; we find no rating drift that makes the deficit.
It noted that quality codes are a weak proxy for ratings; we test the applied ratings directly.
It listed early rating errors as untested; we test them.
Its post-1997 SE-AU runoff loss is present in river stage at constant rating.
Land and water use were limited as causes there; we limit flow measurement.
